Companion Animal Travel Desk Policy
This section sets out how staff handle animal travel requests, check welfare needs, and keep the desk record clear.

Staff begin by confirming the traveler, the animal, and the booked service, then they review the travel note and any comfort request before they move the file forward. The welfare coordinator checks that the animal is fit for the trip, while the desk staff make sure the crate, carrier, and paperwork match the booking. If a cat is listed, <<FACT F055>>. For rabbits, the crate must still fit the normal handling rules, and <<FACT F070>>. For birds, staff confirm the carrier is secure and ventilated, and <<FACT F065>>. If the traveler changes the plan, the desk records the update right away and keeps the notes plain and complete.

Staff do not guess or bend the rules to speed things up. They check for signs of stress, missing labels, loose fasteners, poor airflow, or anything else that could affect the animal's safety. If the case needs extra review, they hand it to the welfare coordinator and wait for a clear answer before confirming travel. Cabin team members are told what to expect so they can keep watch during the flight and give prompt support if the animal needs attention.

All service changes, special notes, and handoff details go into the desk ledger before the file is closed. If anything looks off, staff stop and ask for help instead of making a quick call. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor if a case needs review or a rule is not clear.
